target.title: fix(ssrf): allow loopback for hostnames in allowedHostnames list (#101965)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SSRF loopback tightening in #100835 blocked loopback addresses for all trusted hostnames, including those explicitly listed in the browser navigation guard's `allowedHostnames`. This broke the contract that explicitly allowed hostnames should bypass SSRF blocking.

The test `allows blocked hostnames when explicitly allowed` fails deterministically:
```
AssertionError: promise rejected "SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address" instead of resolving
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` only allowed loopback for explicit loopback hostnames (`localhost`, `127.x.x.x`, `::1`). Hostnames in the SSRF policy's `allowedHostnames` list were treated as trusted for DNS resolution but still blocked if they resolved to loopback addresses.

The fix passes the SSRF policy to the function so it can check `allowedHostnames` in addition to explicit loopback hostnames.

## User Impact

- Browser navigation guard's explicit hostname allowlist works correctly again
- Hostnames in `allowedHostnames` that resolve to loopback (e.g. `agent.internal` -> `127.0.0.1`) are permitted
- Metadata/link-local addresses remain blocked for all trusted hostnames
- No change for non-allowlisted hostnames

## Evidence

- 26/26 tests pass in navigation-guard.test.ts (previously 1 failed)
- 52/52 tests pass in ssrf.test.ts
- Format clean (oxfmt)

Fixes #101965
